text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Maltese press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Former top shareholder of the Bical Bank, which failed in 1972, says controller has enough funds to settle all distributions to depositors.

- 16 nominations for Malta Drydocks Council election. Workers in the state-owned yard will vote later this month to elect four workers to sit on the yard's managing council. The council was set up in 1975 and was wholly constituted of members elected by dockyard workers until amendments to the Dockyard Law earlier this month which provide for the government to nominate a majority of the members, including the chairman. The amendments were made to enable the government to tackle the yard's mounting losses.

- Medical Association presents report to the government saying Malta should have one general hospital rather than having services split in two. The association says a new hospital, still in the initial stages of construction, should be extended to take in all facilities while the existing, 60-year-old hospital should be converted into an old people's home. The government is considering whether to continue the new hospital project, started by the previous Nationalist government
- Irish President Mary Robinson in Malta on a private visit.
- Nationalist Party accuses the government of putting local councils in financial squeeze.
